summary:
Orbital Fire Lab is an interactive web platform designed to [simulate combustion behavior in microgravity / monitor and predict orbital wildfire patterns using NASA satellite data]. By combining real-time visualization with accessible scientific modeling, our solution helps [researchers and students understand how fire behaves differently in space / emergency responders detect and analyze thermal anomalies from orbit].

How It Works & Key Features:

Interactive Simulation / Visualization: Users can manipulate key environmental variables—such as [gravity levels, oxygen concentration, airflow / satellite thermal layers and historical fire datasets]—to observe real-time changes in flame dynamics and spread.

NASA Data Integration: Built using [NASA FIRMS / Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) / ISS combustion experiment datasets] to ground every simulation in authentic orbital telemetry.

Accessible Web Interface: Engineered as a lightweight, browser-based lab so anyone can explore space-based fire science without specialized hardware.
details:
1. The Challenge & Problem Fire behaves fundamentally differently in microgravity than on Earth—without buoyancy-driven convection, flames become spherical, burn longer at lower temperatures, and produce unexpected toxic byproducts. Understanding and visualizing these dynamics is critical for crew safety on long-duration space missions (such as the ISS, Lunar Gateway, and Mars transit), yet real experimental data is often locked behind complex research papers or specialized simulation software.

2. Our Solution: Orbital Fire LabOrbital Fire Lab is an interactive, browser-based scientific simulator and visualization platform that brings space combustion science to students, researchers, and engineers. Through a clean, real-time interface, users can test how fire responds to extraterrestrial conditions without needing supercomputers or specialized lab equipment.

3. Key Features & How It Works

  • Interactive Environment Controls: Users can adjust critical variables in real time—such as gravity levels ($1g$ Earth, $0.16g$ Moon, $0.38g$ Mars, and $0g$ microgravity), oxygen concentration, cabin airflow/ventilation, and fuel/material types—to immediately observe changes in flame shape, spread rate, and temperature.
  • Real-Time Telemetry & Data Visualization: Dynamic charts and live readouts display combustion metrics (heat release rate, flame radius, oxygen consumption, and soot/gas emissions) as parameters change.
  • Guided Scenarios & Comparisons: Built-in presets allow side-by-side comparison between terrestrial fire behavior and spacecraft cabin conditions.

4. NASA Data & Scientific Grounding Our simulation parameters and validation baselines are grounded in open NASA research and datasets, including:

  • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) / Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI): Reference data from International Space Station (ISS) combustion experiments such as FLARE, Saffire (Spacecraft Fire Experiment), and FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment).
  • NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS): Empirical models on microgravity flame spread, limiting oxygen index (LOI) in spacecraft atmospheres, and fire suppression thresholds.

5. Tech Stack

  • Frontend & UI: React, TypeScript/JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, deployed on Vercel.
  • Simulation & Graphics Engine: [HTML5 Canvas / Three.js / WebGL / custom physics equations] for real-time flame rendering and thermodynamic calculations.
  • Data Visualization: [Chart.js / Recharts / D3] for live telemetry plotting.

6. Impact & Future Scope Orbital Fire Lab bridges the gap between raw NASA microgravity research and interactive STEM education. In future iterations, we aim to integrate multi-compartment spacecraft airflow modeling, custom CAD cabin imports, and automated fire-suppression strategy testing.
